description: Computer-use operability audit (x-grok 18, prompts/finish/040). Before = scripts/audit-agent-operability.mjs run against the pre-fix src/avatar-page.js and pages/forge.html (git HEAD). After = the same audit run against the fixed source. Both runs drive /create, /forge, /connect, an agent profile chat, and /launch using only Playwright getByRole/getByLabel locators; /launch is read-only and never clicks the signing button.
fixesApplied: src/avatar-page.js: the agent-chat message textarea had no accessible name; added aria-label="Message {agent name}" so getByLabel(/Message/i) resolves it.

src/avatar-page.js: the assistant chat bubble showed "Thinking..." with no live-region wiring while a reply streamed in; it is now role=status aria-live=polite, so the wait is announced instead of silent.
pages/forge.html: #result-label (the generation-complete label src/forge.js writes into) had no role/aria-live; added role=status aria-live=polite so completion is announced, not just visually shown.
knownEnvironmentConditions: agent-chat's /api/chat call is returning 503 rate_limited ("The AI chat is at capacity right now") from this machine right now, independently reproduced by direct curl against providers groq and vertex-gemini over several minutes. This is a live backend LLM-capacity condition, not a frontend defect: the page already surfaces it as visible, accessible chat text (see lastReply below), and src/shared/log.js's error level is designed to always print so a real backend failure is never silently swallowed. Out of scope for this accessibility-focused order.

forge's GPU worker cold-start/queue time varied 20s-220s+ across runs on this shared machine during testing. The audit script now tracks the per-second #gen-meta elapsed ticker alongside the stage copy so a long but actively-updating wait is recorded as slow-backend (informational), not stalled (a defect); it is only a hard failure if the status text goes fully static for over 60s with no result or error.
